content:
The [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. What money will be worth — or cost — in future years. Enter your amount today, annual inflation rate and years and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Inflation steadily reduces what your money can buy. This calculator shows how much the same basket of goods will cost in future, and how much today's money will be worth. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the Inflation Calculator

Start by entering your amount today, then entering your annual inflation rate (%) and finally entering your years. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your amount today.
2. Enter your annual inflation rate (%).
3. Enter your years.
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Future cost = Amount × (1 + inflation)^years. Purchasing power = Amount ÷ (1 + inflation)^years.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. At 3% inflation, something costing 1,000 today will cost about 1,343.92 in 10 years. Try the same figures in the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Amount today: 1000, Annual inflation rate: 3 %, Years: 10), the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) returns Future cost of the same goods: 1,343.92, Future purchasing power: 744.09, Cumulative inflation: 34.39%. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Aim for investments that beat inflation after tax.
- Cash savings lose real value when interest is below inflation.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a normal inflation rate?

Many central banks target about 2% per year. Try it with your own numbers in the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How does inflation affect savings?

If your savings earn less than inflation, their real value falls each year. Try it with your own numbers in the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Inflation Calculator use?

Future cost = Amount × (1 + inflation)^years. Purchasing power = Amount ÷ (1 + inflation)^years. You can see it in action in the [Inflation Calculator](/inflation-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Inflation Calculator?

Just Amount today, Annual inflation rate and Years. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
